correctness.rationale: Conditioning on the new type yields p_A=q(1-y)/(1+(1-2q)y) and p_B=q(1+y)/(1-(1-2q)y), so their average is f_q(y)=q+b y²/(1-a²y²), b=2q(1-q)(1-2q). The fourth-moment summability of y_j makes the quartic Taylor remainder converge in L²; for a fair-walk imbalance T_n=sum S_j²/(j+2)², E T_n=log n+O(1) and Var T_n=4 log n+O(1). Subsequence Borel-Cantelli and monotonicity give a.s. T_n/log n->1. A bounded-increment martingale representation yields sqrt(log n) Gaussian compensator fluctuations; the edge martingale has bracket nq(1-q)+o(n), while the mixed bracket is O(log n)/sqrt(nlog n)->0. Thus the joint normal limits are independent; q=1/2 and hard-choice binomial cases follow exactly. Independently recomputed q=1/4,y=1/3 rational predictor f=19/70 and cross bracket -9/70.
